title: rosa communis subsp. canina
intro: Rosa communis subsp. canina, commonly known as Dog Rose or Wild Rose, is a plant species from the Rosaceae family, native to Europe, Western Asia, and North Africa. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, helping to soothe digestive issues, reduce fever, and alleviate skin conditions. The therapeutic actions of Rosa communis subsp. canina include its ability to calm digestive disorders, lower blood pressure, and exhibit antiseptic and antiviral properties. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and essential oils, which contribute to its medicinal and therapeutic effects.
